370.subject: Botany
370.text:
Assertion : Movement of materials inside phloem is bidirectional i.e. it can be both upwards or downwards.
Reason : Movement of molecules inside xylem is unidirectional i.e. always upwards.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
370.sol: Long distance bulk movement of substances that occurs through conducting or vascular tissues of plants is called translocation. There are two vascular tissues, xylem and phloem. Xylem translocation is mainly from roots to aerial parts. It passes water with mineral salts, some organic nitrogen and hormones i.e. unidirectional. Phloem translocates organic substances and inorganic solutes first from leaves to all other parts of the plant and storage organs. Storage organs re-export organic nutrients to those parts which require the same as newly formed leaves and fruits i.e it is bidirectional.

2010.text:
Assertion : Diabetes insipidus is marked by excessive urination and too much thirst of water.
Reason : Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) is secreted by the posterior lobe of pituitary gland.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2010.sol: Antidiuretic hormone $(\mathrm{ADH})$ or vasopressin is secreted from posterior pituitary gland. It is released in response to a fall in the water content of blood plasma and leads to an increase in the permeability to water of the distal and collecting tubules of the nephron. Deficiency or hyposecretion of $\mathrm{ADH}$ results in diabetes insipidus. Diabetes insipidus is characterised by micturating dilute urine several times a day which results in excessive thirst (polydipsia) and dehydration.

4720.text: Which one of the following reactions does not take place?
4720.sol:
The reaction, $\mathrm{Br}_2+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Br}^{-}+\mathrm{Cl}_2$ does not take place as the $E_{\text{red }}^{\circ}$ of the above reaction is comes out to be negative. Thus, the reaction is non-spontaneous.

Half cell reaction are given as
At cathode, $\mathrm{Br}_2+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Br}^{-} ; E_{\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{Br}^{-}}^{\circ}=1.09 \mathrm{~V}$
At anode, $2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl}_2+2 e^{-} ; E_{\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{Cl}^{-}}^{\circ}=1.36 \mathrm{~V} \therefore E_{\text{red }}^{\circ}=E_{\text{cathode }}^{\circ}-E_{\text{anode }}^{\circ} \Rightarrow(1.09-1.36) \mathrm{V} \Rightarrow-0.27 \mathrm{~V}$
But the $E_{\text{red }}^{\circ}$ values of other reaction are comes out to be positive. Thus, the all other reaction can take place.

$f(x)=x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}=\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)+2, g(x)=x-\frac{1}{x}$
Let $x-\frac{1}{x}=tf(x)=t^2+2, g(x)=t\begin{aligned} & \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=t+\frac{2}{t}=h(t) \\ & h^{\prime}(t)=1-\frac{2}{t^2}\end{aligned}$
On putting $h^{\prime}(t)=0\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & 1-\frac{2}{t^2} & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & t & = \pm \sqrt{2} \\ \Rightarrow & & h^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{4}{t^3}\end{aligned}h^{\prime \prime}(-\sqrt{2}) < 0$ and $h^{\prime \prime}(\sqrt{2}) > 0\therefore t=\sqrt{2}$ is a point of minima. Local minimum value of $h(t)=\sqrt{2}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=2 \sqrt{2}\therefore$ Required local minimum value
$=2 \sqrt{2}$

10303.text: If a five digit number divisible by 3 is to be formed using the numbers $0,1,2,3,4$ and 5 without repetition, then the total number of ways this can be done is
10303.sol:
Any number is divisible by 3 if sum of its all digit is divisible by 3. (i) Sum when digits are $0,1,2,3,4=10$ not divisible by 3 (ii) Sum when digits are $0,1,2,3,5=11$ not divisible by 3 (iii) Sum when digits are $0,1,2,4,5=12$ divisible by 3 So, number of 5 digit numbers with $0,1,2,4,5$ are $4 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1=96$ (iv) Sum when digits are $0,1,3,4,5=13$ not divisible by 3 (v) Sum when digits are $0,2,3,4,5=14$ not divisible by 3 (vi) Sum when digits are $1,2,3,4,5=15$ divisible by 3
So, number of 5 digit numbers with $1,2,3,4,5$ are $5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1=120$. Thus, required no. of ways $=96+120=216$.

19724.text: An organic compound [X] (Molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_2$ ) reacts with dil. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ to form an alcohol [B] and a carboxylic acid [C]. Reaction of compound $[\mathrm{B}]$ with Jones reagent yielded compound $[\mathrm{C}]$. When compound $[\mathrm{C}]$ was heated with $\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ an Anhydride was formed. Compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ is ________.
19724.sol:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_2$ corresponds to an ester. Hydrolysis of an ester $\mathrm{RCOOR}'$ with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ yields a carboxylic acid $\mathrm{RCOOH}$ and an alcohol $\mathrm{R}'\mathrm{OH}$.

Given that the alcohol [B] is oxidized by Jones reagent to the carboxylic acid [C], it implies that the alcohol [B] and the acid [C] must contain the same number of carbon atoms. Since the total number of carbons in the ester is 6, the acid and the alcohol must each contain 3 carbons.

The acid [C] is propanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$) and the alcohol [B] is propan-1-ol ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$).

The ester [X] formed from propanoic acid and propan-1-ol is propyl propanoate, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COO} \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_3$.

Reviewing the provided options, option (ag53o) represents $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COO} \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_3$, which is propyl propanoate. Heating propanoic acid with $\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ yields propanoic anhydride, consistent with the problem statement.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{COO}-\left(\mathrm{CH}_2\right)_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$

20329.text: What would be the major product formed in the reaction?
20329.sol:
$(CH_3)_3CO^-$ is a bulky base. With bulky bases, E2 elimination is favoured over substitution, and the less hindered (Hofmann) product is preferred.

The substrate is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2Cl$. The only $\beta$-hydrogen available (on the carbon bearing $CH_3$) is abstracted by the bulky base, giving elimination.

The major product is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH_2$ (2-methylpropene), formed by E2 elimination of HCl.

Option (2) is correct.

21251.text: $\text{ If } I_n=\int_\limits0^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan ^n x d x \text{, for } n \geq 2 \text{, then } I_n+I_{n-2}=$
21251.sol:
Given $I_n = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan^{n} x dx$.

Consider the sum $I_n + I_{n-2} = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan^{n} x dx + \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan^{n-2} x dx$.

$I_n + I_{n-2} = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan^{n-2} x (\tan^{2} x + 1) dx$.

Using the identity $\tan^{2} x + 1 = \sec^{2} x$, we have:

$I_n + I_{n-2} = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} \tan^{n-2} x \sec^{2} x dx$.

Let $u = \tan x$, then $du = \sec^{2} x dx$.

When $x = 0$, $u = 0$. When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $u = 1$.

$I_n + I_{n-2} = \int_{0}^{1} u^{n-2} du$.

$I_n + I_{n-2} = \left[ \dfrac{u^{n-1}}{n-1} \right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{n-1}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{n-1}$

22008.subject: Mathematics
22008.text: If the sum of 12th and 22nd terms of an AP is 100, then the sum of the first 33 terms of an $\mathrm{AP}$ is
22008.sol:
Let the first term of the arithmetic progression be $a$ and the common difference be $d$. The $n$-th term of an AP is given by $T_n = a + (n-1)d$.

The 12th term is $T_{12} = a + 11d$ and the 22nd term is $T_{22} = a + 21d$.

Given $T_{12} + T_{22} = 100$, we have $(a + 11d) + (a + 21d) = 100$, which simplifies to $2a + 32d = 100$. Dividing by 2, we get $a + 16d = 50$.

The sum of the first $n$ terms of an AP is given by $S_n = \dfrac{n}{2} [2a + (n-1)d]$.

For $n = 33$, the sum is $S_{33} = \dfrac{33}{2} [2a + (33-1)d] = \dfrac{33}{2} [2a + 32d]$.

Substituting $2a + 32d = 100$ into the expression for $S_{33}$, we get $S_{33} = \dfrac{33}{2} \times 100 = 33 \times 50 = 1650$.

Answer: 1650

22130.subject: Mathematics
22130.text: The ratio in which the line $3 x+4 y+2=0$ divides the distance between the lines $3 x+4 y+5=0$ and $3 x+4 y-5=0$ is
22130.sol:
The given lines are parallel, represented by the equations $3x + 4y + 5 = 0$, $3x + 4y + 2 = 0$, and $3x + 4y - 5 = 0$.

Let the lines be $L_1: 3x + 4y + 5 = 0$, $L_2: 3x + 4y + 2 = 0$, and $L_3: 3x + 4y - 5 = 0$.

The distance between two parallel lines $ax + by + c_1 = 0$ and $ax + by + c_2 = 0$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$.

The distance $d_1$ between $L_1$ and $L_2$ is $d_1 = \dfrac{|5 - 2|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

The distance $d_2$ between $L_2$ and $L_3$ is $d_2 = \dfrac{|2 - (-5)|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}} = \dfrac{7}{5}$.

The ratio in which $L_2$ divides the distance between $L_1$ and $L_3$ is $d_1 : d_2 = \dfrac{3}{5} : \dfrac{7}{5} = 3 : 7$.

Answer: 3 : 7

22598.subject: Physics
22598.text: The mobility of the charge carriers increases with
options: Decrease in the charge of the mobile carriers
Increase in the mass of the charge
22598.sol:
The mobility $\mu$ of charge carriers in a conductor is defined as the ratio of the drift velocity $v_d$ to the applied electric field $E$.

The expression for drift velocity is $v_d = \dfrac{eE\tau}{m}$, where $e$ is the charge of the carrier, $\tau$ is the average relaxation time (average collision time), and $m$ is the mass of the carrier.

Substituting this into the definition of mobility: $\mu = \dfrac{v_d}{E} = \dfrac{e\tau}{m}$.

From the relation $\mu = \dfrac{e\tau}{m}$, it is evident that the mobility $\mu$ is directly proportional to the average collision time $\tau$. Therefore, mobility increases as the average collision time increases.

Answer: The average collision time

23031.subject: Physics
23031.text: A circular coil of radius $0.1 \mathrm{ m}$ is placed in the $\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{Y}$ plane and a current $2 \mathrm{ A}$ is passed through the coil in the clockwise direction when looking from above. Find the magnetic dipole moment of the current loop
23031.sol:
The magnetic dipole moment $\vec{m}$ of a current loop is given by the formula $\vec{m} = I \vec{A}$, where $I$ is the current and $\vec{A}$ is the area vector.

The radius of the coil is $r = 0.1 \text{ m}$. The area of the circular coil is $A = \pi r^2 = \pi (0.1)^2 = 0.01 \pi \text{ m}^2$.

The current $I = 2 \text{ A}$. The magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment is $m = I A = 2 \times 0.01 \pi = 0.02 \pi \text{ Am}^2$.

The coil is placed in the X-Y plane. According to the right-hand rule, for a clockwise current when viewed from above (looking down the positive Z-axis), the direction of the area vector $\vec{A}$ is along the negative Z-axis. Therefore, the magnetic dipole moment $\vec{m}$ is directed in the negative Z-direction.

Answer: $0.02 \pi \mathrm{Am}^2 \text{ in the }-\mathrm{ve} \mathrm{ Z}-\text{ direction }$

24121.subject: Mathematics
24121.text:
Consider the following sets of points in the complex plane
$A = \left\{ \cos\left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\right) : n \in \mathbb{Z} \right\}$ and
$B = \left\{ \cos\left(\dfrac{2n}{5}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{2n}{5}\right) : n \in \mathbb{Z} \right\}$.
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: $A$ is infinite and $B$ is also infinite.
$A$ is finite and $B$ is also finite.
24121.sol:
The set $A$ consists of complex numbers of the form $z_n = \cos\left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\right) = e^{i \dfrac{2n\pi}{5}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Since $e^{i \dfrac{2(n+5)\pi}{5}} = e^{i \dfrac{2n\pi}{5}} \cdot e^{i 2\pi} = e^{i \dfrac{2n\pi}{5}}$, the values repeat after every $5$ integers. Thus, $A$ contains exactly $5$ distinct elements, making $A$ a finite set.

The set $B$ consists of complex numbers of the form $w_n = \cos\left(\dfrac{2n}{5}\right) + i\sin\left(\dfrac{2n}{5}\right) = e^{i \dfrac{2n}{5}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

If two elements in $B$ are equal, then $e^{i \dfrac{2n_1}{5}} = e^{i \dfrac{2n_2}{5}}$ for some $n_1, n_2 \in \mathbb{Z}$.

This implies $\dfrac{2n_1}{5} - \dfrac{2n_2}{5} = 2k\pi$ for some $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

$n_1 - n_2 = 5k\pi$

Since $n_1, n_2, k$ are integers and $\pi$ is an irrational number, the equality holds if and only if $k = 0$, which gives $n_1 = n_2$.

Therefore, all elements in $B$ corresponding to distinct integers $n$ are distinct. Thus, $B$ contains infinitely many elements, making $B$ an infinite set.

Answer: $A$ is finite but $B$ is infinite.

24189.subject: Mathematics
24189.text:
Let $r, l$ be two integers such that $r \geq l \geq 3$. What is the total number of functions
$f : \{1, 2, \ldots, r\} \rightarrow \{1, 2, \ldots, r\}$
such that $f(1), f(2), \ldots, f(l)$ are all distinct?
24189.sol:
The total number of elements in the domain is $r$ and in the codomain is $r$.

We need to find the number of functions such that the images of the first $l$ elements, $f(1), f(2), \ldots, f(l)$, are all distinct.

The number of ways to choose distinct images for these $l$ elements from the $r$ available elements in the codomain is given by ^{r}P_{l}$:

^{r}P_{l} = r(r-1)(r-2)\cdots(r-l+1)$

For the remaining $r-l$ elements in the domain, there are no restrictions. Each of these elements can be mapped to any of the $r$ elements in the codomain.

The number of ways to assign images to these remaining $r-l$ elements is $r^{r-l}$.

The total number of such functions is the product of these two quantities:

Total functions $= r(r-1)(r-2)\cdots(r-l+1) \times r^{r-l}$

$= r^{r-l+1}(r-1)(r-2)\cdots(r-l+1)$

Answer: $r^{r-l+1}(r-1)(r-2)\cdots(r-l+1)$

One mole of an ideal gas at $300K$ in thermal contact with its surroundings expands isothermally from $1 . 0L to 2 . 0L$ against a constant pressure of $3 . 0atm$. In this process, the change in entropy of the surroundings $\left(∆ {S}_{surr}\right) in J{K}^{- 1}$ is:
$\left(1Latm = 101 . 3J\right)$
25174.sol:
From ${1}^{st}$ law of thermodynamics,
${q}_{sys} = ∆ U - w = 0 - \left[- {P}_{ext} . ∆ V\right]$
$= 3.0atm \times \left(2.0L - 1.0L\right) = 3.0Latm$
$∴ ∆ {S}_{surr} = \dfrac{{\left({q}_{rev}\right)}_{surr}}{T} = - \dfrac{{q}_{sys}}{T}$
$= - \dfrac{3.0 \times 101.3J}{300K}$
$= - 1 .013 J / K$
Alternate solution:
$∆ {S}_{surr} = \dfrac{{q}_{surr}}{T} = - \dfrac{{q}_{sys}}{T} = \dfrac{{W}_{sys}}{T}$
$∵$ For the isothermal process:
$∆ U = 0$ ${q}_{sys} = - {W}_{sys}$
$∆ {S}_{surr.} = \dfrac{- {P}_{ext}\left({V}_{f} - {V}_{i}\right)}{T}$
$= \dfrac{- 3 ( 2 - 1 )}{300} \times 101.3$
$= - 1.013J / K$

$\because f^{\prime}(x)>0 \forall x \in[0,2)$ and $f^{\prime}(x) < 0 \forall x \in(2,3)$

26816.subject: Chemistry
26816.text:
One mole of phenol is treated with dilute HNO$_3$ at $298$ K to give a mixture of products. The mixture is separated by steam distillation. The steam volatile compound (X) is separated. The increase in percentage of oxygen in (X) with respect to phenol is _____ $\times 10^{-1}$ %
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H:$1$, C:$12$, N:$14$, O:$16$)
26816.sol:
When phenol is treated with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ at $298\text{ K}$, it undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution to give a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol.

The mixture is separated by steam distillation. Ortho-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas para-nitrophenol is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Thus, the steam volatile compound (X) is ortho-nitrophenol.

Molecular formula of phenol: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{O}$
Molar mass of phenol $= (6 \times 12) + (6 \times 1) + 16 = 94\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Percentage of oxygen in phenol $= \dfrac{16}{94} \times 100 \approx 17.02\%$

Molecular formula of ortho-nitrophenol (X): $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_3$
Molar mass of ortho-nitrophenol $= (6 \times 12) + (5 \times 1) + 14 + (3 \times 16) = 139\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Percentage of oxygen in ortho-nitrophenol $= \dfrac{48}{139} \times 100 \approx 34.53\%$

Increase in percentage of oxygen $= 34.53\% - 17.02\% = 17.51\%$

We need to express this as $y \times 10^{-1} \%$.
$17.51\% = 175.1 \times 10^{-1} \%$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $175$.

Answer: $175$

${BeCl}_{2} \to sp$

${CH}_{4} \to {sp}^{3}$

34497.text:
Let $N$ denote the number that turns up when a fair die is rolled. If the probability that the system of equations

$x + y + z = 12x + Ny + 2z = 23x + 3y + Nz = 3$

has unique solution is $\dfrac{k}{6},$ then the sum of value of $k$ and all possible values of $N$ is
34497.sol:
Given equations are

$x + y + z = 12x + Ny + 2z = 23x + 3y + Nz = 3$

So,

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & N & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & N\end{cases}\right|$

Applying ${C}_{2} ↔ {C}_{2} - {C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{3} ↔ {C}_{3} - {C}_{1}$

$⇒ ∆ = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & N - 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & N - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ ∆ = \left(N - 2\right)\left(N - 3\right)$

For unique solution $∆ \ne 0$, so

$N \ne 2, 3$

Also, $N \in \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\right\}$ and for unique solution $N$ can take values $\left\{1, 4, 5, 6\right\}$.

$⇒ P$(system has unique solution ) $= \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{k}{6}$

So, $k = 4$

Therefore, required sum is

$= 4 + 1 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20$

36177.text: Let the point $P$ be the vertex of the parabola $y = x^2 - 6x + 12$. If a line passing through the point $P$ intersects the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 4y + 3 = 0$ at the points $R$ and $S$, then the maximum value of $(PR + PS)^2$ is :
36177.sol:
The equation of the parabola is $y = x^2 - 6x + 12$, which can be rewritten as $y - 3 = (x - 3)^2$.

The vertex of the parabola is $P(3, 3)$.

The equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 4y + 3 = 0$, which can be rewritten as $(x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 2$.

The center of the circle is $C(1, 2)$ and its radius is $r = \sqrt{2}$.

The distance between the point $P$ and the center $C$ is:

$PC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (3 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 1} = \sqrt{5}$

Since $PC = \sqrt{5} > r = \sqrt{2}$, the point $P$ lies outside the circle.

Let the line through $P$ intersect the circle at $R$ and $S$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of the chord $RS$. The perpendicular distance from the center $C$ to the chord is $CM$.

Using the right-angled triangle $\triangle PCM$, the distance from $P$ to the midpoint $M$ is $PM = \sqrt{PC^2 - CM^2}$.

The lengths of the segments are $PR = PM - RM$ and $PS = PM + RM$.

Therefore, the sum of the distances is:

$PR + PS = (PM - RM) + (PM + RM) = 2PM = 2\sqrt{PC^2 - CM^2}$

To maximize $(PR + PS)^2$, we need to maximize $PC^2 - CM^2$. This occurs when $CM$ is minimized, which means $CM = 0$. This happens when the line passes through the center $C$ of the circle.

Substituting $CM = 0$, we get the maximum sum:

$PR + PS = 2PC = 2\sqrt{5}$

Thus, the maximum value of $(PR + PS)^2$ is:

$(2\sqrt{5})^2 = 4 \times 5 = 20$

Answer: $20$

36716.text: In a game, a man wins Rs. $100$ if he gets $5$ or $6$ on a throw of a fair die and loses Rs. $50$ for getting any other number on the die. If he decides to throw the die either till he gets a five or a six or to a maximum of three throws, then his expected gain/loss (in rupees) is :
36716.sol:
Probability of success i.e. getting a $5$ or $6 = P\left(s\right) = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

So, probability of failure i.e. getting any number other than $5$ or $6 = P\left(f\right) = 1 - P\left(s\right) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Let $X$ be the amount that a man wins in a maximum of three throws.

So, $X$ can take values :

Case I : First two throws are $5$ or $6$, game stops

$⇒ X = 100 ⇒ P\left(X = 100\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Case II : First throw is other than $5$ or $6$ and second and third throws are $5$ or $6$, game stops

$⇒ X = 50 ⇒ P\left(X = 50\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{9}$

Case III : First two throws are other than $5$ or $6$ and last throw is $5$ or $6$

$⇒ X = 0 ⇒ P\left(X = 0\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{27}$

Case IV : All three throws are other than $5$ or $6$

$⇒ X = - 150 ⇒ P\left(X = - 150\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{8}{27}$

Therefore, expected gain or loss

$= E\left(X\right) = 100 \times \dfrac{1}{3} + 50 \times \dfrac{2}{9} + 0 \times \dfrac{4}{27} - 150 \times \dfrac{8}{27} = 0$

36888.sol:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation

${x}^{2} + \left(3 - a\right)x + 1 - 2a = 0$

Then, sum of roots $\alpha + \beta = a - 3$

And product of roots $\alpha\beta = 1 - 2a$

We know that ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = {\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 2\alpha\beta$

$∴ {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = {\left(a - 3\right)}^{2} - 2\left(1 - 2a\right)$

$= {a}^{2} - 2a + 7$

$= {\left(a - 1\right)}^{2} + 6$

$∴$ Minimum value of ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = 6$ at $a = 1$.

38446.text: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors such that $|\vec{a}| = 2$ and $|\vec{b}| = 3$, then the maximum value of $3\left|\left(3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\right)\right| + 4\left|\left(3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}\right)\right|$ is :
38446.sol:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.

We have $|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9|\vec{a}|^2 + 4|\vec{b}|^2 + 12|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta}$

Substituting $|\vec{a}| = 2$ and $|\vec{b}| = 3$:

$|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9(4) + 4(9) + 12(2)(3)\cos\theta} = \sqrt{36 + 36 + 72\cos\theta}$

$|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{72(1+\cos\theta)} = \sqrt{144\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)} = 12\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

Similarly, $|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9|\vec{a}|^2 + 4|\vec{b}|^2 - 12|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta}$

$|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{36 + 36 - 72\cos\theta} = \sqrt{72(1-\cos\theta)} = \sqrt{144\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)} = 12\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

The given expression becomes:

$3|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| + 4|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = 3\left(12\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right) + 4\left(12\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)$

$= 36\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) + 48\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

The maximum value of $A\cos x + B\sin x$ is $\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$.

Maximum value $= \sqrt{36^2 + 48^2} = \sqrt{1296 + 2304} = \sqrt{3600} = 60$

Answer: $60$

43440.subject: Physics
43440.text: Find the correct combination of $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and D inputs which can cause the LED to glow.
43440.sol:
The LED will glow if it is forward biased, which means the potential at the p-side must be higher than the potential at the n-side.
Let $Y_1$ be the output of the upper NAND gate (p-side) and $Y_2$ be the output of the lower NOR gate (n-side).
For the LED to glow, we need $Y_1 = 1$ and $Y_2 = 0$.
The upper circuit consists of two NOT gates (NOR gates with shorted inputs) followed by a NAND gate.
Output of first NOT gate is $\bar{A}$, and second is $\bar{B}$.
$Y_1 = \overline{\bar{A} \cdot \bar{B}} = \overline{\bar{A}} + \overline{\bar{B}} = A + B$ (using De Morgan's Law).
The lower circuit is a NOR gate with inputs $C$ and $D$.
$Y_2 = \overline{C + D}$.
Condition 1: $Y_1 = 1 \implies A + B = 1$. This means at least one of $A$ or $B$ must be 1.
Condition 2: $Y_2 = 0 \implies \overline{C + D} = 0 \implies C + D = 1$. This means at least one of $C$ or $D$ must be 1.
Checking the options:
(1) $A=1, B=1, C=0, D=1$: $Y_1 = 1+1 = 1$ and $Y_2 = \overline{0+1} = 0$. (Satisfied)
(2) $A=0, B=0, C=1, D=1$: $Y_1 = 0+0 = 0$. (Not satisfied)
(3) $A=1, B=0, C=0, D=0$: $Y_2 = \overline{0+0} = 1$. (Not satisfied)
(4) $A=0, B=1, C=0, D=0$: $Y_2 = \overline{0+0} = 1$. (Not satisfied)
Thus, the correct combination is 1101.
43440.meta: Find the correct combination of A, B, C and D inputs which can cause the LED to glow.

44208.subject: Physics
44208.text: In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4 mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness $20 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by $\frac{\alpha}{10}$, where $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
44208.sol:
In Young's Double Slit Experiment, when a thin transparent sheet of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is introduced in front of one slit, the central bright fringe shifts by a distance $\Delta y$.
The formula for the shift is given by $\Delta y = \frac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t$.
Given values:
Distance between slits $d = 0.4\text{ mm} = 0.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$
Distance to screen $D = 1\text{ m}$
Thickness of sheet $t = 20\mu\text{m} = 20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$
Shift $\Delta y = 20\text{ mm} = 20 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$
Substituting the values into the formula:
$20 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{1}{0.4 \times 10^{-3}} \times (\mu - 1) \times 20 \times 10^{-6}$
$20 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{20 \times 10^{-6}}{0.4 \times 10^{-3}} \times (\mu - 1)$
$20 \times 10^{-3} = 50 \times 10^{-3} \times (\mu - 1)$
$\mu - 1 = \frac{20}{50} = 0.4$
$\mu = 1.4$
The refractive index is given as $\frac{\alpha}{10}$.
So, $1.4 = \frac{\alpha}{10}$
$\alpha = 14$

In the case of formation of nucleus the evolution of energy equals to the binding energy of the nucleus takes place due to disappearance of a fraction of total mass. If the quantity of mass disappearing is $\Delta m$, then the binding energy is
$B E=\Delta m c^2$
cFrom the above discussion, it is clear that the mass of the nucleus must be less than the sum of the masses of the constituent neutrons and protons. We can then write
$\Delta m=Z m_p-N m_n-m(A, Z)$
where $m(A, Z)$ is the mass of the atom of mass number $A$ atomic number $Z$. Hence, the binding energy of nucleus is
$\begin{aligned} & B E=\left[Z m_p+N m_n-m(A, Z)\right] c^2 \\ & B E=\left[Z m_p+(A-Z) m_n-m(A, Z)\right] c^2\end{aligned}$

54240.text: An electric kettle has two coils. When one coil is switched on, it takes 10 min to boil water and when the second coil is switched on it takes 20 min to boil same amount of water. The time taken by electric kettle to boil water when-both coil are used in parallel, is found to be $n$ second. Find the value of $n$.
54240.sol:
Heat produced in a resistance $R$ in time $t$ is given by
$H=\frac{V^2}{R} t[\text{ where }, V=\text{ source voltage }]$
For first coil,
$H_1=\frac{V^2}{R_1} t_1=\frac{V^2}{R_1} \times 10 \times 60 \left[\because t_1=10 \times 60 \mathrm{~s}\right]$
For second coil, $H_2=\frac{V^2}{R_2} t_2 \left[\because t_2=20 \times 60 \mathrm{~s}\right]$
$=\frac{V^2}{R_2} \times 20 \times 60$
Given that, $H_1=H_2$
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \frac{V^2}{R_1} \times 10 \times 60=\frac{V^2}{R_2} \times 20 \times 60 \\
\Rightarrow & R_2=2 R_1..(i)
\end{array}$
Let $t$ be the time taken by electric kettle to boil water when both coil are used in parallel, then
$\begin{aligned}
H_p= & \left(\frac{V^2}{R_1}+\frac{V^2}{R_2}\right) \times t=V^2 t\left(\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{2 R_1}\right)[\text{ from Eq. (i) }] \\
& H_p=\frac{3 V^{2}t}{2 R_1}
\end{aligned}$
But, $H_P=H_1$
$\therefore \frac{3 V^2 t}{2 R_1}=\frac{V^2}{R_1} \times 10 \times 60$
$\Rightarrow t=400 \mathrm{~s}$

55247.subject: Chemistry
55247.text: Which from following compounds is obtained when propionamide is treated with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH solution ?
55247.sol:
Propionamide is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction of an amide with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH is known as the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

In this reaction, the amide is converted into a primary amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{KBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The product obtained is ethylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

56295.subject: Chemistry
56295.text: Identify an aldehyde used in margarine and in food for its buttery odour.
56295.sol:
The correct answer is (2) Butyraldehyde.
Butyraldehyde (also known as butanal) is an aldehyde that has a characteristic buttery odor. It is commonly used in the food industry to impart a buttery flavor, and it is also found in margarine to enhance its aroma.
Here's a quick look at the other options:
- (1) Benzaldehyde: This aldehyde has an almond-like aroma and is used in flavorings and perfumes, but not for a buttery odor.
- (3) Cinnamaldehyde: This aldehyde is responsible for the characteristic flavor and aroma of cinnamon, not butter.
- (4) Oxaldehyde: This is not a common aldehyde and does not fit the description related to buttery odors.
Thus, Butyraldehyde is the aldehyde associated with the buttery scent in margarine and other food products.

56420.subject: Chemistry
56420.text: What is EAN of Co in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$?
56420.sol:
The effective atomic number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{O.S.} + 2 \times \text{C.N.}$

For the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, the central metal is cobalt.

Atomic number of Co ($Z$) = $27$

Oxidation state of Co ($\text{O.S.}$) = $+3$

Coordination number ($\text{C.N.}$) = $6$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\text{EAN} = 27 - 3 + 2 \times 6$

$\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$

Answer: $36$

60555.subject: Mathematics
60555.text: The area bounded by the curves $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = -|x| + 1$ is
60555.sol:
The given curves are $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = -|x| + 1$.

To find the points of intersection, we equate the two equations:

$|x| - 1 = -|x| + 1$

$2|x| = 2 \Rightarrow |x| = 1 \Rightarrow x = \pm 1$

The required area $A$ is the region bounded between these two curves from $x = -1$ to $x = 1$.

$A = \int_{-1}^{1} [(-|x| + 1) - (|x| - 1)] dx$

$A = \int_{-1}^{1} (2 - 2|x|) dx$

Since the integrand is an even function:

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{1} (2 - 2x) dx$

$A = 2 \left[ 2x - x^2 \right]_{0}^{1}$

$A = 2 (2 - 1) = 2$ sq. units.

Answer: $2$ sq. units

61030.subject: Mathematics
61030.text: The value of $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x(1 + \sin x)}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$ is...
61030.sol:
Let $I = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x(1 + \sin x)}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Splitting the integral, we get:

$I = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx + \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

The first integral is zero because the integrand $f(x) = \dfrac{2x}{1 + \cos^2 x}$ is an odd function.

The second integral has an even integrand, so:

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Using the property $\int_{0}^{a}f(x)dx = \int_{0}^{a}f(a-x)dx$, we get:

$I = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi - x) \sin(\pi - x)}{1 + \cos^2(\pi - x)}dx = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi - x) \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Adding the two expressions for $I$:

$2I = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\pi \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

$I = 2\pi \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Substituting $\cos x = t$, we get $-\sin x dx = dt$. The limits change from $1$ to $-1$:

$I = 2\pi \int_{1}^{-1}\dfrac{-dt}{1 + t^2} = 2\pi \int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{dt}{1 + t^2}$

$I = 2\pi [\tan^{-1} t]_{-1}^{1} = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} -\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)

$I = $2\pi \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi^2$

Answer: \pi^2

62549.subject: Mathematics
62549.text: If $\cot(\cos^{-1} x) = \sec \left(\tan^{-1} \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}\right), then the value of $ x$ is$
62549.sol:
Let $\cos^{-1} x = \theta \Rightarrow \cos \theta = x$

$\cot \theta = \dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

Let $\tan^{-1} \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}} = \phi \Rightarrow \tan \phi = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}$

$\sec \phi = \sqrt{1 + \tan^2 \phi} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{a^2}{b^2 - a^2}} = \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}$

Given $\cot \theta = \sec \phi$, we have:

$\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}$

Squaring both sides:

$\dfrac{x^2}{1 - x^2} = \dfrac{b^2}{b^2 - a^2}$

$x^2(b^2 - a^2) = b^2(1 - x^2)$

$x^2 b^2 - x^2 a^2 = b^2 - x^2 b^2$

$x^2(2b^2 - a^2) = b^2$

$x^2 = \dfrac{b^2}{2b^2 - a^2}$

$x = \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{2b^2 - a^2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{b}{\sqrt{2b^2 - a^2}}$

Given: Evaluate $E = \tan \left(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}} - \sin^{-1}\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\right).

Let $ A = \cos^{-1}$\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}} and $ B = \sin^{-1}$\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}, so $ E = \tan(A - B)$.

Since \cos A = \frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}} >0$ and $A$ lies in $[0, \pi], we have \sin A > 0$ and can determine the opposite side: \sqrt{(5\sqrt{2})^2 - 1^2} =$7$. Thus, $\tan A = 7$.

Similarly, $\sin B = \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} >0$ and $B$ lies in $[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}], so \cos B > 0$ and the adjacent side is \sqrt{(\sqrt{17})^2 - 4^2} =$1$. Therefore, $\tan B = 4$.

Apply the identity $\tan(A - B) = \frac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A \tan B}.

$ E = $\frac{7 - 4}{1 + 7 \cdot 4} = \frac{3}{29}

The value is \frac{3}{29}, so the answer is $\boxed{$\text{C}$}$.

$

64428.text: A triangle ABC is formed by $\mathrm{A}(1,-1,0), \mathrm{B}(3,5,3), \mathrm{C}(-11,-5,6)$. The equation of internal angle bisector of angle $A$ is
64428.sol:
Given triangle vertices $A(1, -1, 0)$, $B(3, 5, 3)$, and $C(-11, -5, 6)$, the position vectors from $A$ are:

$\vec{AB} = (2, 6, 3)$, with magnitude $7$
$\vec{AC} = (-12, -4, 6)$, with magnitude $14$

The unit vectors are $\hat{u}_{AB} = \left(\frac{2}{7}, \frac{6}{7}, \frac{3}{7}\right)$ and $\hat{u}_{AC} = \left(-\frac{6}{7}, -\frac{2}{7}, \frac{3}{7}\right)$.

The direction vector of the angle bisector is given by their sum:

$\vec{d} = \hat{u}_{AB} + \hat{u}_{AC} = \left(-\frac{4}{7}, \frac{4}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\right)

Multiplying by $7$ yields the proportional vector $(-4, 4, 6)$, which simplifies to $(-2, 2, 3)$ when divided by $2$.

The bisector line passes through $A(1, -1, 0)$ with this direction, giving the equation:

\frac{x - 1}{-2} = \frac{y + 1}{2} = \frac{z}{3}

This is equivalent to \frac{1 - x}{2} = \frac{y + 1}{2} = \frac{z}{3}, which matches option A.

Final answer: \boxed{A}$

The dot product is $\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b} = |\overline{a}| |\overline{b}| \cos\theta = 15 \cdot \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -10$.

65880.subject: Physics
65880.text:
If ' m ' is the mass of electron, ' V ' is its velocity, ' r ' is the radius of stationary circular orbit around a nucleus with charge 'Ze' then from Bohr's first postulate the kinetic energy of the electron is
$\left(\mathrm{K}=1 / 4 \pi \epsilon_0\right)$
65880.sol:
The kinetic energy of an electron in a stationary circular orbit is derived from Bohr's first postulate, where the centripetal force equals the electrostatic attraction.

The electrostatic force between nucleus charge $Ze$ and electron charge $e$ is $F_e = K\frac{Ze^2}{r^2}$ with $K = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$.
The centripetal force for circular motion is $F_c = \frac{mV^2}{r}$.

Setting $F_c = F_e$ yields $\frac{mV^2}{r} = K\frac{Ze^2}{r^2}$.
Multiplying both sides by $r$ gives $mV^2 = K\frac{Ze^2}{r}$.

Kinetic energy is $KE = \frac{1}{2}mV^2 = \frac{1}{2}K\frac{Ze^2}{r}$.

$KE = \frac{KZe^2}{2r}$ corresponds to option A.

65883.text: In Paschen series, wavelength of first line is ' $\lambda_1$ ' and for Brackett series, wavelength of first line is ' $\lambda_2$ ' then ratio $\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}$ is
65883.sol:
The Rydberg formula gives the wavelength of spectral lines as

$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right)

where $R$ is the Rydberg constant and $n_i \gt n_f$.

For the first line of the Paschen series ($n_f = 3$, $n_i = 4$):

\frac{1}{\lambda_1} =$R $\left( \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = R \left( \frac{7}{144} \right)$

Hence $\lambda_1 = \frac{144}{7R}$.

For the first line of the Brackett series ($n_f = 4$, $n_i = 5$):

$\frac{1}{\lambda_2} = R \left( \frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{25} \right) =$R $\left( \frac{9}{400} \right)

Thus $\lambda_2 = $\frac{400}{9R}.

The ratio becomes

\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \frac{144}{7R} \times \frac{9R}{400} = \frac{1296}{2800}

Simplifying by dividing numerator$ and $denominator by 16 yields \frac{81}{175}.

This corresponds to option C.

$

66776.text: Two coils P and Q have mutual inductance 'M' H. If the current in the coil P is $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$, then the maximum value of e.m.f. induced in coil Q is
66776.sol:
The induced e.m.f. in coil Q due to the current in coil P is given by

$e = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$

Given $I = I_0 \sin \omega t$, differentiating with respect to time $t$ gives

$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = I_0 \omega \cos \omega t$

Substituting this into the expression for induced e.m.f.,

$e = -M I_0 \omega \cos \omega t$

The maximum value of the induced e.m.f. corresponds to the maximum magnitude of $\cos \omega t$, which is $1$.

$e_{\text\max} = M \omega I_0$

Given a gravitational potential energy $E = \frac{GMm}{R}$, where $M$ is Earth's mass, $m$ is the body's mass, and $G$ is the gravitational constant, we find that $GMm = ER$.

The weight at distance $1.5R$ equals the gravitational force there: $W' = \frac{GMm}{(1.5R)^2}$.

Substituting $GMm = ER$ yields $W' = \frac{ER}{(1.5R)^2} = \frac{ER}{2.25R^2} = \frac{E}{2.25R}$.

Since $2.25 = \frac{9}{4}$, this simplifies to $W' = \frac{4E}{9R}$, corresponding to option C.

68516.text: Two stones of masses m and 3 m are whirled in horizontal circles, the heavier one in a radius $\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{3}\right)$ and lighter one in a radius r . The tangential speed of lighter stone is ' $n$ ' times the value of heavier stone. When the magnitude of centripetal force becomes equal the value of $n$ is
68516.sol:
The centripetal forces are equal: $F_L = F_H$. For stones with masses $m_L = m$, $m_H = 3m$ and radii $r_L = r$, $r_H = \frac{r}{3}$, with tangential speeds related by $v_L = n v_H$, the force equality becomes:

$\frac{m (n v_H)^2}{r} = \frac{3m v_H^2}{r/3}$

Simplifying both sides yields:

$\frac{m n^2 v_H^2}{r} = \frac{9m v_H^2}{r}$

Canceling common factors ($m$, $v_H^2$, and $r$) from both sides gives $n^2 = 9$, so $n = 3$.

Answer: $\boxed{3}$

69439.subject: Physics
69439.text: Which of the following graph represents the temperature (T) dependence of resistivity ($\rho$) of a semiconductor?
69439.sol:
The resistivity of a semiconductor is given by the relation:
$\rho = \rho_0 e^{\dfrac{E_g}{2k_B T}}$
where $E_g$ is the band gap energy, $k_B$ is the Boltzmann constant, and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

As the temperature $T$ increases, the number density of charge carriers (electrons and holes) increases exponentially because more electrons gain enough thermal energy to jump from the valence band to the conduction band. Consequently, the resistivity $\rho$ decreases exponentially with an increase in temperature.

Graph (B) correctly represents this non-linear (exponential) decrease of resistivity with temperature.

Answer: B

vibrate in S.H.M. of different periods and different amplitudes
70453.sol:
The equation of a stationary wave is given by $y = 2A \sin(kx) \cos(\omega t)$.

This can be written as $y = A' \cos(\omega t)$, where $A' = 2A \sin(kx)$ is the amplitude of the particle at position $x$.

The amplitude $A'$ depends on the position $x$, meaning different particles vibrate with different amplitudes.

The time-dependent part $\cos(\omega t)$ is the same for all particles, indicating that they all vibrate in Simple Harmonic Motion (S.H.M.) with the same angular frequency $\omega$ and the same period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$.

At the nodes, $\sin(kx) = 0$, so the amplitude is zero and the particles do not vibrate.

Therefore, all particles except those at the nodes vibrate in S.H.M. with the same period but different amplitudes.

Answer: except at node vibrate in S.H.M. of same period but of different amplitudes

71454.subject: Biology
71454.text:
Given below are two statements regarding anaerobic respiration in the muscles.
Statement (I): In muscles, NADH+H^+ produced during glycolysis is reoxidised to NAD.
Statement (II): One proton and two electrons produced, which are donated to pyruvic acid which yields lactic acid leading to muscle fatigue.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71454.sol:
Statement (I) is correct because during anaerobic respiration in muscle cells (lactic acid fermentation), the NADH + H^+$ produced during glycolysis is reoxidised to NAD^+$ to ensure a continuous supply of NAD^+$ for glycolysis to proceed.

Statement (II) is incorrect because during the reduction of pyruvic acid to lactic acid, NADH + H^+$ donates two protons (2$H^+$) and two electrons (2$e^-$) to pyruvic acid, not one proton and two electrons. The reaction is catalysed by lactate dehydrogenase.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71573.subject: Biology
71573.text: According to the proton transport theory of stomatal mechanism, protons are formed in guard cells when ____.
options: starch is converted into sugar during night time
sugar is converted into starch during the day time.
Potassium malate is formed during the night time
Malic acid dissociates to form malate during day time
71573.sol:
According to the active potassium ion transport theory (proton transport theory) proposed by Levitt, stomatal opening during the daytime is driven by the accumulation of potassium ions in the guard cells.

During the daytime, starch in the guard cells is converted into malic acid. Malic acid then dissociates into malate anions and protons (H^+$).

These protons are actively pumped out of the guard cells into the surrounding subsidiary cells, and in exchange, potassium ions (K^+$) are transported into the guard cells. The potassium ions combine with malate to form potassium malate, which increases the osmotic concentration of the guard cells, leading to endosmosis and stomatal opening.

Thus, protons are formed in the guard cells when malic acid dissociates to form malate during the daytime.

Answer: Malic acid dissociates to form malate during day time
71573.meta: According to the proton transport theory of stomatal mechanism, protons are formed in guard cells when ____.

71653.text: Aniline undergoes diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2$/HCl to give compound A. Compound A reacts with fluoroboric acid to give compound B. When B is heated with aq. $\text{NaNO}_2$ in the presence of copper, it forms compound C. Identify C.

Aniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming benzenediazonium chloride (Compound A).

$\text{Ar}-\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{Ar}-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ (A)

Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with fluoroboric acid ($\text{HBF}_4$) to yield benzenediazonium fluoroborate (Compound B).

$\text{Ar}-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{HBF}_4} \text{Ar}-\text{N}_2^+\text{BF}_4^-$ (B)

When benzenediazonium fluoroborate is heated with aqueous $\text{NaNO}_2$ in the presence of copper, the diazonium group is replaced by a nitro group, forming nitrobenzene (Compound C).

$\text{Ar}-\text{N}_2^+\text{BF}_4^- \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2, \text{Cu}, \Delta} \text{Ar}-\text{NO}_2$ (C)

Thus, Compound C is $\text{Ar}-\text{NO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{Ar} - \text{NO}_2$

72298.subject: Physics
72298.text: Two cars, P and Q move toward each other, getting $8\ \text{m}$ closer every second. If they move in the same direction, they get $0.6\ \text{m}$ closer every second. If car P is faster than car Q then, the ratio of speeds of car P to car Q is
72298.sol:
Let the speeds of car P and car Q be $v_P$ and $v_Q$ respectively, and $v_P > v_Q$.

When the cars move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. Since they get $8\ \text{m}$ closer every second:

$v_P + v_Q = 8$

When the cars move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds. Since they get $0.6\ \text{m}$ closer every second:

$v_P - v_Q = 0.6$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$2v_P = 8.6 \Rightarrow v_P = 4.3\ \text{m/s}$

Subtracting the second equation from the first, we get:

$2v_Q = 7.4 \Rightarrow v_Q = 3.7\ \text{m/s}$

The ratio of the speeds of car P to car Q is:

$\dfrac{v_P}{v_Q} = \dfrac{4.3}{3.7} = \dfrac{43}{37}$

Answer: $43:37$

77853.subject: Mathematics
77853.text: What is the number of selections of at most 3 things from 6 different things?
77853.sol:
The number of ways to select $r$ things from $n$ different things is given by ^{n}C_{r}$.

The phrase "at most 3 things" means we can select 0, 1, 2, or 3 things from the 6 available different things.

The total number of selections is the sum of these possibilities:

^{6}C_{0} + ^{6}C_{1} + ^{6}C_{2} + ^{6}C_{3}$

Calculating each term:

^{6}C_{0} = 1$

^{6}C_{1} = 6$

^{6}C_{2} = $\dfrac{6 \times 5}{2 \times 1} =15$

^{6}C_{3} = $\dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4}{3 \times 2 \times 1} =20$

Total number of selections = 1 + 6 + 15 + 20 = 42$.

Answer: 42$

77984.subject: Mathematics
77984.text: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability that two heads do not occur consecutively?
77984.sol:
Total number of possible outcomes when a fair coin is tossed 4 times is $2^4 = 16$.

Let $E$ be the event that two heads do not occur consecutively. The favorable outcomes are the sequences of length 4 that do not contain 'HH'.

We can count these by the number of heads in the sequence:
Case 1: $0$ heads
TTTT ($1$ outcome)

Case 2: $1$ head
HTTT, THTT, TTHT, TTTH ($4$ outcomes)

Case 3: $2$ heads
To avoid consecutive heads, the heads must be separated by tails. The possible arrangements are HTHT, HTTH, THTH ($3$ outcomes)

Case 4: $3$ or $4$ heads
It is impossible to place $3$ or $4$ heads in $4$ tosses without at least two heads being consecutive. ($0$ outcomes)

Total number of favorable outcomes = $1 + 4 + 3 = 8$.

Required probability = $\dfrac{8}{16} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $1/2$

79970.text:
A lake near a village suffered heavy mortality of fishes within a few days. Consider the following reasons for this
(1) Lots of urea and phosphate fertilizer were used in the crops in the vicinity.
(2) The area was sprayed with DDT by an aircraft.
(3) The lake water turned green and stinky.
(4) Phytoplankton populations in the lake declined initially thereby greatly reducing photosynthesis.
Which two of above were the main causes of fish mortality in the lake?
79970.sol:
The heavy mortality of fishes in the lake within a span of few days is due to Eutrophication.
Eutrophication is the phenomenon of nutrient enrichment of nitrogen and phosphorus in a water body that supports a dense growth of plants and animal life. Due to nutrient enrichment, excess growth of algae occurs which is called algal bloom. When these algae die, their organic matter gets decomposed and this results in the depletion of oxygen leading to death of aquatic animals. Hence, this indicates that lot of urea and phosphate fertilizers are were used in nearby crops. The lake water could have turned green and stinky due to excess growth of Algae.

81110.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
81110.text: Among the following options, the correct trend in the electron gain enthalpy is
81110.sol:
The electron gain enthalpy generally becomes less negative as we move down a group due to the increase in atomic size.

However, fluorine has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than chlorine. This is because fluorine has a very small atomic size, leading to strong interelectronic repulsions in the compact $2p$ subshell. As a result, the incoming electron experiences less attraction from the nucleus compared to chlorine.

The values of electron gain enthalpy for halogens are approximately:
$\text{Cl} = -349 \text{ kJ/mol}$
$\text{F} = -328 \text{ kJ/mol}$
$\text{Br} = -325 \text{ kJ/mol}$
$\text{I} = -295 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Considering the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy, the correct trend is $\text{Cl} > \text{F} > \text{Br} > \text{I}$.

Answer: $\text{Cl}>\text{F}>\text{Br}>\text{I}$

Which of the following statements are correct?

(i) Centre of mass of a body always coincides with the centre of gravity of the body.

(ii) Centre of mass of a body is the point at which the total gravitational torque on the body is zero

(iii) A couple on a body produce both translational and rotational motion in a body.

(iv) Mechanical advantage greater than one means that small effort can be used to lift a large load.
82296.sol:
(i) Centre of gravity coincides with centre of mass for bodies when gravitational field is uniform (usually for bodies of small height).

(ii) Since the gravitational force can be assumed to be centred at the centre of gravity, so torque of gravitational force about the centre of gravity must be zero. In mechanics, usually we deal with the objects of small height for which torque of gravitational force about centre of mass will also be zero.

(iii) Couple produces only rotational motion.

(iv) Mechanical advantage $= \dfrac{Load}{Effort} > 1$ $⇒ Load > Effort$

$60$ cm to the left of the concave lens
$30$ cm to the right of the concave lens
83319.sol:
For the first lens $L_1$ (convex lens):
Object distance, $u_1 = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f_1 = +10$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 1}{30} = \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +15$ cm
The image $I_1$ formed by $L_1$ acts as a virtual object for the second lens $L_2$.

For the second lens $L_2$ (concave lens):
Distance between the lenses, $d = 3$ cm
Object distance for $L_2$, $u_2 = v_1 - d = 15 - 3 = +12$ cm
Focal length, $f_2 = -10$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{-10}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{5 - 6}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v_2 = -60$ cm

The negative sign indicates that the final image is formed $60$ cm to the left of the concave lens.

Answer: $60$ cm to the left of the concave lens

85519.text: Identify the tissue shown in the diagram and match with its characteristics and its location.
options: Smooth muscles, show branching, found in the wall of the heart.
Cardiac muscles, unbranched muscles, found in the walls of the heart.
Striated muscles, tapering at bothends, attached with the bones of the ribs.
Skeletal muscles show striations and are closely attached with the bones of the limbs.
85519.sol:
Skeletal muscles show alternate light and dark bands or striations and hence called striated muscles. The cells of this tissue are long, cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate (having many nuclei). Smooth or involuntary muscles are unstriated muscles. The cells are long with pointed ends (spindleshaped) and uninucleate (having a single nucleus). Cardiac muscles or Heart muscle cells are cylindrical, branched and uninucleate. They are involuntary in nature.
Related Theory Muscular tissue consists of elongated cells, also called muscle fibres. This tissue is responsible for movement in our body. Muscles contain special proteins called contractile proteins, which contract and relax to cause movement.

100914.subject: Physics
100914.text: An object with an initial kinetic energy of $15\text{ J}$ is acted upon simultaneously by two constant forces $\vec{F}_1 = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k})\text{ N}$ and $\vec{F}_2 = (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\text{ N}$. Under the influence of these forces, the object moves from an initial point $A(1, 2, -1)\text{ m}$ to a final point $B(3, 4, 2)\text{ m}$. The final kinetic energy of the object is
100914.sol:
First, find the net force acting on the object by adding the individual forces:
$\vec{F}_{net} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2$
$\vec{F}_{net} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) = (6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})\text{ N}$

Next, determine the displacement vector by subtracting the initial position coordinates from the final position coordinates:
$\Delta\vec{r} = \vec{r}_B - \vec{r}_A$
$\Delta\vec{r} = (3 - 1)\hat{i} + (4 - 2)\hat{j} + (2 - (-1))\hat{k} = (2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k})\text{ m}$

Calculate the net work done using the dot product of net force and displacement:
$W = \vec{F}_{net} \cdot \Delta\vec{r}$
$W = (6)(2) + (2)(2) + (1)(3) = 12 + 4 + 3 = 19\text{ J}$

Finally, apply the work-energy theorem to find the final kinetic energy:
$W = K_f - K_i$
$19 = K_f - 15$
$K_f = 15 + 19 = 34\text{ J}$

Answer: $34\text{ J}$

102078.subject: Physics
102078.text:
An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process A $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ C $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A, which forms a rectangle on a Pressure (P) versus Volume (V) diagram. The sides AB and CD are parallel to the volume axis, while BC and DA are parallel to the pressure axis. The volume of the gas increases during the process A $\rightarrow$ B.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Process A $\rightarrow$ B(I) Positive work
(B) Process B $\rightarrow$ C(II) Negative work
(C) Process C $\rightarrow$ D(III) Zero work
(D) Net cycle A $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ C $\rightarrow$ D $\rightarrow$ A

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102078.sol:
In a P-V diagram, the work done by a gas is the area under the process curve on the volume axis.

For the process A $\rightarrow$ B, the line is parallel to the volume axis (isobaric) and the volume increases. Since it is an expansion, the work done is positive.

For the process B $\rightarrow$ C, the line is parallel to the pressure axis (isochoric). The volume is constant ($\Delta V = 0$), so the work done is zero.

For the process C $\rightarrow$ D, the process is isobaric and the volume decreases to return to the initial volume coordinate. Since it is a compression, the work done is negative.

The net work done in a cyclic process is the area enclosed by the cycle on the P-V diagram. Since the expansion A $\rightarrow$ B occurs at a higher pressure than the compression C $\rightarrow$ D, the cycle is clockwise and the net work done by the gas is positive.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

102445.subject: Physics
102445.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the amplitude of a simple harmonic oscillator is doubled, the area enclosed by its velocity-displacement graph becomes two times its original value.

Reason (R): The velocity-displacement graph of a simple harmonic oscillator is an ellipse whose semi-major and semi-minor axes are both directly proportional to the amplitude.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
102445.sol:
The velocity $v$ of a simple harmonic oscillator at displacement $x$ is given by $v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$, which can be rewritten as $\dfrac{v^2}{(\omega A)^2} + \dfrac{x^2}{A^2} = 1$.

This is the equation of an ellipse in the $x$-$v$ plane. The semi-axes of this ellipse are $A$ (along the $x$-axis) and $\omega A$ (along the $v$-axis). Both axes are directly proportional to the amplitude $A$. Thus, Reason (R) is true.

The area enclosed by the ellipse is given by $\pi \times (\text{semi-major axis}) \times (\text{semi-minor axis}) = \pi (A)(\omega A) = \pi \omega A^2$.

Since the area is proportional to $A^2$, doubling the amplitude will make the area four times its original value, not two times. Thus, Assertion (A) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

102919.text:
Match the electrostatic configurations involving infinitely long straight wires with uniform linear charge density $\lambda$ in List-I with the magnitude of the net electric field at the specified point in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Midpoint between two parallel wires with charge densities $+\lambda$ and $+\lambda$ separated by a distance $2R$(I) Zero
(B) Midpoint between two parallel wires with charge densities $+\lambda$ and $-\lambda$ separated by a distance $2R$(II) $\dfrac{\lambda}{\pi\epsilon_0 R}$
(C) A point at a perpendicular distance $R$ from a single wire with charge density $+\lambda$(III) $\dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R}$
(D) A point at a perpendicular distance $2R$ from a single wire with charge density $+\lambda$(IV) $\dfrac{\lambda}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102919.sol:
For A: The electric fields due to the two identical wires at the midpoint are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Net electric field is zero. (A matches I)

For B: The electric fields due to the two wires at the midpoint are in the same direction. Net electric field $E = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R} + \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R} = \dfrac{\lambda}{\pi\epsilon_0 R}$. (B matches II)

For C: The electric field at a distance $R$ from a single infinite line charge is $E = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R}$. (C matches III)

For D: The electric field at a distance $2R$ from a single infinite line charge is $E = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 (2R)} = \dfrac{\lambda}{4\pi\epsilon_0 R}$. (D matches IV)

Answer: (A) $\rightarrow$ (I), (B) $\rightarrow$ (II), (C) $\rightarrow$ (III), (D) $\rightarrow$ (IV)

104364.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: The phase difference of two light waves change if they travel through different media having same thickness, but different indices of  refraction.

Reason R: The wavelengths of waves are different in different media.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
104364.sol:
When light travels through a medium, its velocity depends on the density of the medium.

The formula to calculate the speed of light can be written as

$v = ν\lambda . . . ( 1 )$

From equation (1), it can be concluded that higher the speed, higher is the wavelength. Hence, the wavelength of light depends on the refractive index of the medium.

Because of changed wavelength the phase difference changes while the two waves travel the same distance.

Thus, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

104487.subject: Physics
104487.text:
An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is constructed using two convex lenses of optical powers $+0.5 \mathrm{~D}$ and $+25 \mathrm{~D}$. Match the parameters of the telescope in List-I with their corresponding values in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Tube length(I) $200 \mathrm{~cm}$
(B) Magnitude of magnifying power(II) $4 \mathrm{~cm}$
(C) Focal length of objective(III) $204 \mathrm{~cm}$
(D) Focal length of eyepiece(IV) $50$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104487.sol:
For an astronomical telescope, the objective lens must have a larger focal length and the eyepiece must have a smaller focal length.

Given powers:
$P_1 = +0.5 \mathrm{~D}$ and $P_2 = +25 \mathrm{~D}$

Focal lengths are:
$f_1 = \dfrac{1}{P_1} = \dfrac{1}{0.5} \mathrm{~m} = 2 \mathrm{~m} = 200 \mathrm{~cm}$
$f_2 = \dfrac{1}{P_2} = \dfrac{1}{25} \mathrm{~m} = 0.04 \mathrm{~m} = 4 \mathrm{~cm}$

Thus, focal length of objective, $f_o = 200 \mathrm{~cm}$ (C $\rightarrow$ I)
Focal length of eyepiece, $f_e = 4 \mathrm{~cm}$ (D $\rightarrow$ II)

In normal adjustment, the tube length is:
$L = f_o + f_e = 200 + 4 = 204 \mathrm{~cm}$ (A $\rightarrow$ III)

Magnitude of magnifying power is:
$|m| = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = \dfrac{200}{4} = 50$ (B $\rightarrow$ IV)

Correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

104696.subject: Physics
104696.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, $10$ fringes are observed in a given segment of the screen when light of wavelength $600\text{ nm}$ is used. When this light is replaced by another monochromatic source, the number of fringes in the same segment of the screen increases by $5$. The wavelength of the new light source is:
104696.sol:
The length of the segment on the screen remains constant. The total width of $n$ fringes is given by $y = n\beta = n\left(\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\right)$.

Since $y$, $D$, and $d$ are constant, $n \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$, which gives $n_1\lambda_1 = n_2\lambda_2$.

The initial number of fringes is $n_1 = 10$ and the initial wavelength is $\lambda_1 = 600\text{ nm}$.

The number of fringes increases by $5$, so the new number of fringes is $n_2 = 10 + 5 = 15$.

Substituting these values into the relation:
$10 \times 600 = 15 \times \lambda_2$
$\lambda_2 = \dfrac{6000}{15} = 400\text{ nm}$.

Answer: $400\text{ nm}$

105585.subject: Physics
105585.text: Three different metals $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ have work functions $2.2\text{ eV}$, $3.1\text{ eV}$ and $4.2\text{ eV}$ respectively. When a monochromatic light beam of energy $E$ is incident on these metals, it is observed that photoelectrons are emitted from metals $X$ and $Y$, but not from metal $Z$. The possible range of the incident photon energy $E$ is:
105585.sol:
For photoelectric emission to occur, the energy of the incident photon must be greater than or equal to the work function of the metal ($E \ge \phi$).

Given work functions: $\phi_X = 2.2\text{ eV}$, $\phi_Y = 3.1\text{ eV}$, $\phi_Z = 4.2\text{ eV}$.

Since metal $X$ emits photoelectrons: $E \ge 2.2\text{ eV}$.
Since metal $Y$ emits photoelectrons: $E \ge 3.1\text{ eV}$.
Since metal $Z$ does not emit photoelectrons: $E < 4.2\text{ eV}$.

To satisfy all three conditions simultaneously, the incident energy must be at least $3.1\text{ eV}$ (to ensure emission from $Y$) but strictly less than $4.2\text{ eV}$ (to prevent emission from $Z$).

Therefore, the possible range is $3.1\text{ eV} \le E < 4.2\text{ eV}$.

Answer: $3.1\text{ eV} \le E < 4.2\text{ eV}$

108640.subject: Chemistry
108640.text: One mole of an ideal gas is allowed to expand freely into an evacuated and thermally insulated vessel. What are the values of the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) and the change in enthalpy ($\Delta H$) for this process?
108640.sol:
The vessel is thermally insulated, which means no heat is exchanged with the surroundings, so $q = 0$.

The gas expands freely into an evacuated vessel, meaning the external pressure is zero ($P_{\text{ext}} = 0$). Therefore, the work done is $w = -P_{\text{ext}}\Delta V = 0$.

From the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is $\Delta U = q + w = 0 + 0 = 0$.

For an ideal gas, the change in enthalpy is given by $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV) = \Delta U + nR\Delta T$.

Since $\Delta U = 0$ for an ideal gas, the change in temperature $\Delta T = 0$. Substituting these values gives $\Delta H = 0 + 0 = 0$.

Hence, both $\Delta U$ and $\Delta H$ are zero.

Answer: $\Delta U = 0$, $\Delta H = 0$

119876.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Guanidine is a much stronger organic base than urea.

Reason (R): The conjugate acid of urea is stabilized by three equivalent resonance structures.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
119876.sol:
Guanidine is a very strong organic base because its conjugate acid (guanidinium ion) is highly stable due to three equivalent resonance structures. Urea is a very weak base because its nitrogen lone pairs are involved in resonance with the electronegative carbonyl oxygen, making them unavailable for protonation. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true.

Reason (R) is false because it is the conjugate acid of guanidine, not urea, that is stabilized by three equivalent resonance structures.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

120857.subject: Chemistry
120857.text:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
a. Deficiency of vitamin $\mathrm{K}$ results in increased blood clotting time.
b. The sources of vitamin $B_2$ are milk and liver
c. Hexapeptide has six peptide bonds
d. Improper functioning of adrenal cortex results in hypoglycemia.
120857.sol:
- a. Deficiency of vitamin K results in increased blood clotting time. This statement is correct. Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of several proteins involved in blood coagulation. A deficiency of this vitamin impairs the body's ability to form blood clots, leading to prolonged clotting time and an increased risk of bleeding.
- b. The sources of vitamin \(B_2\) are milk and liver. This statement is correct. Vitamin \(B_2\), also known as riboflavin, is found in a variety of foods, with rich sources including dairy products like milk and organ meats like liver.
- c. Hexapeptide has six peptide bonds. This statement is incorrect. A hexapeptide is a peptide chain composed of six amino acids. The number of peptide bonds in a polypeptide chain is always one less than the number of amino acids. Therefore, a hexapeptide has five peptide bonds.
- d. Improper functioning of the adrenal cortex results in hypoglycemia. This statement is correct. The adrenal cortex produces glucocorticoids, such as cortisol, which help regulate blood sugar levels by promoting gluconeogenesis. Hypofunction of the adrenal cortex, as see in Addison's disease, leads to a deficiency of these hormones, which can result in a dangerously low blood glucose level, or hypoglycemia.
Based on this analysis, the correct statements are \(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}\), and \(\mathrm{d}\). The correct option is (4).

123600.subject: Botany
123600.text: What is the purpose of kinetochores?
options: To move the chromosomes towards opposite poles
123600.sol: The kinetochores are the site where microtubules attach to the chromosomes, pulling the chromosomes towards opposite poles of the cell during mitosis. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell. Hence, the metaphase is characterised by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.

123892.subject: Botany
123892.text:
Arrange the following events of Prophase I of meiosis in their correct chronological order:

(A) Recognition of X-shaped chiasmata
(B) Compaction of chromosomes
(C) Appearance of recombination nodules
(D) Assembly of meiotic spindle
(E) Formation of synaptonemal complex

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
123892.sol:
The correct chronological order of the stages of Prophase I is Leptotene $\rightarrow$ Zygotene $\rightarrow$ Pachytene $\rightarrow$ Diplotene $\rightarrow$ Diakinesis.

1. Leptotene: Compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this stage (B).
2. Zygotene: Homologous chromosomes start pairing together, accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex (E).
3. Pachytene: This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs (C).
4. Diplotene: The synaptonemal complex dissolves, and the recombined homologous chromosomes separate except at the sites of crossovers, forming X-shaped structures called chiasmata (A).
5. Diakinesis: The final stage is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata and the assembly of the meiotic spindle to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation (D).

Therefore, the correct sequence is (B), (E), (C), (A), (D).

Answer: (B), (E), (C), (A), (D)

125153.text: Which of the following sets of enzymes and complexes is exclusively located in or on the inner mitochondrial membrane?
options: Succinate dehydrogenase, Cytochrome $c$ oxidase, ATP synthase
125153.sol:
Succinate dehydrogenase (Complex II), Cytochrome $c$ oxidase (Complex IV), and ATP synthase (Complex V) are all physically located in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Pyruvate dehydrogenase and most enzymes of the TCA cycle (such as citrate synthase and $\alpha$-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase) are located in the mitochondrial matrix.

Enzymes of glycolysis (such as hexokinase, phosphofructokinase, pyruvate kinase, and enolase) are found in the cytoplasm.

Porins are large protein channels found in the outer mitochondrial membrane.

Answer: Succinate dehydrogenase, Cytochrome $c$ oxidase, ATP synthase

125800.subject: Botany
125800.text: What is distinct in the transverse section of an anther?
125800.sol: Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca. Let us understand the various types of tissues and their organisation in the transverse section of an anther The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains.

125860.subject: Botany
125860.text: What type of division does the nucleus of the functional megaspore undergo?
125860.sol: Let us study about the formation of the embryo sac in detail. The nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to form two nuclei which move to the opposite poles, forming the 2- nucleate embryo sac. Two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions result in the formation of the 4-nucleate and later the 8-nucleate stages of the embryo sac. It is of interest to note that these mitotic divisions are strictly free nuclear, that is, nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation. After the 8-nucleate stage, cell walls are laid down leading to the organisation of the typical female gametophyte or embryo sac. Observe the distribution of cells inside the embryo sac Six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls and organised into cells; the remaining two nuclei, called polar nuclei are situated below the egg apparatus in the large central cell. There is a characteristic distribution of the cells within the embryo sac.

127135.subject: Botany
127135.text: What is the most conservative and scientifically sound estimate of the global species diversity?
127135.sol: For many taxonomic groups, species inventories are more complete in temperate than in tropical countries. Considering that an overwhelmingly large proportion of the species waiting to be discovered are in the tropics, biologists make a statistical comparison of the temperate-tropical species richness of an exhaustively studied group of insects and extrapolate this ratio to other groups of animals and plants to come up with a gross estimate of the total number of species on earth. Some extreme estimates range from 20 to 50 million, but a more conservative and scientifically sound estimate made by Robert May places the global species diversity at about 7 million.

127158.subject: Botany
127158.text: How many species of birds does India have?
127158.sol: The diversity of plants and animals is not uniform throughout the world but shows a rather uneven distribution. For many group of animals or plants, there are interesting patterns in diversity, the most well- known being the latitudinal gradient in diversity. In general, species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles. With very few exceptions, tropics (latitudinal range of 23.5° N to 23.5° S) harbour more species than temperate or polar areas. Colombia located near the equator has nearly 1,400 species of birds while New York at 41° N has 105 species and Greenland at 71° N only 56 species. India, with much of its land area in the tropical latitudes, has more than 1,200 species of birds.
127158.meta: How many species of birds does India have?

127923.text: What is the role of the pancreas in frogs?

The body cavity of frogs accommodate different organ systems such as digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, excretory and reproductive systems with well developed structures and functions The digestive system consists of alimentary canal and digestive glands. 128793.subject: Zoology
128793.text: What is the function of basophils in the body?
options: Destroy foreign organisms entering the body
Resisting infections and associated with allergic reactions
128793.sol: Leucocytes are also known as white blood cells (WBC) as they are colorless due to the lack of haemoglobin. They are nucleated and are relatively lesser in number which averages 6000-8000 mm–3 of blood. Leucocytes are generally short lived. We have two main categories of WBCs – granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and basophils are the least (0.5-1 per cent) among them. Neutrophils and monocytes (6-8 per cent) are phagocytic cells which destroy foreign organisms entering the body. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory reactions. Eosinophils (2-3 per cent) resist infections and are also associated with allergic reactions. Lymphocytes (20-25 per cent) are of two major types – ‘B’ and ‘T’ forms. Both B and T lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses of the body.

129065.subject: Zoology
129065.text: During the cardiac cycle, as ventricular systole is initiated, the pressure inside the ventricles increases. Which of the following sets of valves close immediately to prevent the backflow of blood into the atria?
129065.sol:
During the cardiac cycle, the initiation of ventricular systole causes ventricular pressure to increase.

This increased pressure forces the closure of the atrio-ventricular (AV) valves to prevent the backflow of blood into the atria. The AV valves are the tricuspid valve (located between the right atrium and right ventricle) and the bicuspid or mitral valve (located between the left atrium and left ventricle).

The semilunar valves close during ventricular diastole, not systole, to prevent backflow from the pulmonary artery and aorta into the ventricles.

Answer: Tricuspid and bicuspid valves

131788.text: In eukaryotes, the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs is catalyzed by which of the following enzymes?
131788.sol:
In eukaryotes, there is a clear division of labor among the RNA polymerases in the nucleus.

RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S).

RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).

RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs (small nuclear RNAs).

DNA-dependent DNA polymerase is involved in DNA replication, not transcription.

Answer: RNA polymerase III

131813.subject: Zoology
131813.text: In a mutant strain of E. coli, a mutation occurs in the $i$ gene of the lac operon, producing a modified repressor protein that has completely lost its ability to bind to the inducer (allolactose). What will be the transcription status of the structural genes ($z$, $y$, and $a$) in this mutant strain?
options: They will be transcribed constitutively, regardless of the presence or absence of lactose.
They will remain permanently switched off in both the presence and absence of lactose.
They will be transcribed normally only when lactose is present in the medium.
They will be transcribed only in the absence of lactose in the medium.
131813.sol:
The $i$ gene synthesises the repressor protein constitutively.

In a normal lac operon, the repressor binds to the operator region and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. When an inducer (lactose or allolactose) is present, it binds to the repressor, altering its conformation and inactivating it, which allows transcription to proceed.

If a mutation causes the repressor to lose its inducer-binding site, the inducer cannot bind to it. As a result, the mutant repressor will remain permanently active and continuously bound to the operator region.

Therefore, RNA polymerase will be permanently blocked, and the structural genes ($z$, $y$, and $a$) will never be transcribed, even if lactose is added to the medium.

Answer: They will remain permanently switched off in both the presence and absence of lactose.

A critical analysis makes us believe that variation due to mutation or variation due to recombination during gametogenesis, or due to gene flow or genetic drift results in changed frequency of genes and alleles in future generation. Coupled to enhance reproductive success, natural selection makes it look like different population. 133095.subject: Zoology
133095.text: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is known to be affected by gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and
133095.sol:
- The Hardy-Weinberg principle states that allele and genotype frequencies in a population will remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of other evolutionary influences.
- When mating is random in a large population with no disruptive circumstances, both genotype and allele frequencies will remain constant because they are in equilibrium.
- Any factor, which can disturb the alleles in a population is likely to affect the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
- The alleles in a population can be altered by mutation, migration, genetic drift, recombination, and natural selection. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is not effected by evolution, limiting factors, saltation and over prediction
So, the correct answer is 'Natural selection'.
